Microsoft's quarterly capital expenditure reached 30.9 billion dollars in the quarter ending March 2026, more than triple the 9.7 billion dollars it reported roughly two years earlier, with no SEC filings recorded alongside that growth.

The climb ran through nearly every reported quarter, 9.7 billion, then 11 billion, then 14.9 billion, then 15.8 billion, then 16.7 billion, then 19.4 billion, then 29.9 billion, then 30.9 billion, with the sharpest single jump landing between the September 2025 and December 2025 quarters, when spending rose by roughly 10.5 billion dollars in one reporting period. That single-quarter acceleration is the largest jump-to-prior-quarter of any builder in this set relative to its own base.

Microsoft's 30.9 billion dollars places it third among the eight builders tracked here, behind Amazon's 54.2 billion and Alphabet's 35.7 billion, and ahead of Meta, Oracle, CoreWeave, Equinix, and Digital Realty. Unlike Amazon, Alphabet, Equinix, and CoreWeave, Microsoft has no SEC filings recorded in this dataset disclosing new financial obligations tied to this spending, which means the growth is visible in reported capex without a corresponding paper trail of individual financing agreements in this collection.
